title: Overlapping source files triple-count matches in standings/team_stats/competition_stats
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp.py:147-151 maps Brasileirao_Matches.csv (2012-2022), novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (2003-2019) AND BR-Football-Dataset.csv (matched via _competition_key) all to competition 'Brasileirao'; standings(2019) returns matches_used=1140 and top team Flamengo with matches=114, points=270 (true Serie A season is 38 matches / 90 pts). Aggregates for overlapping seasons are ~3x inflated.
suggestion: Deduplicate matches across source files (by date+teams+score) or restrict each competition/season to a single authoritative source before computing standings/stats.

title: Standings/stats display uses raw un-canonicalized team names
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp.py:307 sets the display name from match['home_team'] (e.g. 'Flamengo-RJ') while grouping by the canonical key; the displayed label depends on which source row was seen first.
suggestion: Store a canonical display name alongside the key so standings show a consistent team label.

title: Test suite asserts consistency but not absolute correctness of standings
evidence: tests/test_brazilian_soccer_mcp.py:29-38 checks W+D+L accounting and point ordering but not match/point counts, so the triple-count bug (F1) passes undetected. test_coverage=0.86, defect_rate=1.0 from scores.json.
suggestion: Add an assertion that a 20-team Brasileirao season yields ~38 matches per team to catch cross-source duplication.
